# Belt noise only when A/C clutch is engaged

A squeal or grind that appears exclusively when the air conditioning compressor engages points directly to a load-dependent mechanical issue. In a vehicle like your 2003 Nissan Primera, the serpentine belt drives multiple accessories, but the compressor adds significant resistance only when its internal solenoid clicks the clutch in. When that resistance spikes, any existing friction or misalignment becomes audible.

Spraying water on the pulley and hearing the sound change confirms that the issue involves the belt-to-pulley interface. Water acts as a temporary lubricant; it reduces the coefficient of friction between the rubber belt and the metal sheave. If the noise disappears or significantly quiets with water, the root cause is almost certainly one of three things: a glazed or hardened belt surface, a misaligned idler or tensioner pulley, or a failing bearing within the compressor itself.

### Diagnosing the Belt Condition

The most common culprit in vehicles of this age is a serpentine belt that has lost its ability to grip under load. Over time, the rubber compounds on the inner ribbed surface can harden or become glazed from heat and friction. A hardened belt acts like a piece of plastic trying to slide over metal rather than rubber gripping metal.

You cannot fix a glazed belt by applying water; you must replace it. However, simply swapping the belt is not always the solution if the underlying geometry is wrong. Before committing to a full replacement, inspect the tensioner arm. If the tensioner feels sloppy or does not maintain consistent pressure, the new belt will slip immediately. You can verify this by pressing down on the tensioner spring; it should offer firm resistance and hold position once released.

### Evaluating Pulley Alignment

Your buyerâs concern about pulley alignment is valid. A misaligned pulley causes the belt to track at an angle, creating uneven wear and increasing the friction surface area against the metal. This extra drag manifests as noise specifically when a high-torque load, like the compressor clutch, is applied.

To check alignment, you need two reference points. Ideally, use another identical vehicle or the factory service manual for your specific Primera to find a known-good pulley setup. If you don't have that, look at the relationship between the crankshaft pulley and the accessory pulleys. They should lie on the same imaginary plane. If one pulley is even slightly off-axis, the belt will rub against the edge of the misaligned sheave when under load.

If the alignment looks correct but the noise persists after a water test, the compressor bearing is likely failing. A worn bearing creates internal drag that increases exponentially once the clutch engages. The water on the outside of the pulley masks the sound by lubricating the external contact point, but it cannot fix the internal mechanical friction inside the compressor housing.

### Replacement Strategy and Trade-offs

If you decide to replace the belt, do not assume a generic aftermarket part will suffice. For a 2003 Primera with a 2L engine, specific routing diagrams are essential because the belt wraps around multiple grooves. Using the wrong belt can cause premature failure or leave components like the power steering pump unpowered.

When replacing the belt, it is highly recommended to replace the tensioner and the idler pulleys simultaneously. These components often suffer from internal bearing wear even if they appear smooth visually. A failing idler pulley bearing creates a whirring noise that can mask or mimic other issues. Replacing all three itemsâthe belt, tensioner, and idlersâprovides a clean slate and ensures the new belt receives proper tension without fighting against worn hardware.

If the diagnosis points to the compressor itself, consider whether rebuilding the unit is more cost-effective than replacing it entirely. However, if the bearing has failed catastrophically, replacement is usually the safer route. Addressing this proactively will give your buyer peace of mind and prevent a roadside breakdown where the belt slips off due to sudden high torque.
